text:
I found no study establishing that independently retrained, ten-interaction NextItNet models outperform full-history models on the four specified Amazon categories with history-length and elapsed-time controls. The strongest NextItNet-specific warning concerns confounding: its authors describe a comparison using length 10 for baselines versus 500 for NextItNet, changing training-example counts and padding costs substantially. Their original comparisons matched session lengths. This supports careful control, not a universal ten-event optimum. [NextItNet authors’ repository](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet)

Adjacent evidence suggests a persistent-interest tradeoff. A SASRec/BERT4Rec study reports stronger performance with longer histories on sparse Amazon Beauty, whereas short histories can remain competitive on dense MovieLens; its reporting does not clearly establish a matched retraining intervention. [Sequence-length study](https://d2j16w31g89z0j.cloudfront.net/site/ictc2025/abs/D05-10.pdf) Time-aware augmentation research finds that interaction-gap distributions matter, so ten events need not represent a consistent temporal horizon. [Uniform Sequence Better](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/25540) RSS separately demonstrates that training-target sampling changes accuracy and convergence, illustrating an optimization explanation for apparent recency gains. [RSS](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/299238/)

Methodological inference: ten interactions is a useful first control, not an established optimum. Retrain short/full NextItNet variants with identical targets, negatives, updates, capacity and validation candidates; restrict context without discarding older training targets. Compare recent-ten against ten chronologically ordered, history-spanning interactions; include full-history regularization controls and inspect convergence. Stratify paired validation differences by available history length, ten-event elapsed span, and last-event-to-target gap. A gain establishes that restricted context helps this training/evaluation protocol; identifying stale-interest removal requires gains beyond matched information-budget, regularization and optimization controls. Older interactions may still help users with persistent interests.
